CHIEF COMPLAINT
Joint pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrew is a 62-year-old male with past medical history significant for kidney transplant, hypothyroidism, and arthritis who presents with bilateral knee pain. Patient reports that over the weekend he was moving boxes up and down basement stairs, and by the end of the day his knees were painful. He reports the pain is equally bilateral and attributes it to repetition and the weight of the boxes. He has had some knee problems in the past. He has tried Tylenol and ice for pain management without significant relief. The pain kept him up Saturday night. He denies fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. He occasionally experiences elbow pain but reports nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reviewed and negative for fever, chills, muscle aches, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and headaches. No other acute symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Kidney transplant (several years ago for polycystic kidney disease)
Hypothyroidism
Arthritis

MEDICATIONS
Immunosuppressive medications
Synthroid
Tylenol as needed

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently moving boxes up and down basement stairs over the weekend

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: normal, afebrile
Heart rate: normal
Blood pressure: normal
Cardiovascular: 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated on heart exam, stable from prior
Right knee: edema and erythema present, pain to palpation, decreased range of motion
Left knee: unremarkable

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: good bony alignment, no acute fracture
Labs: white blood cell count not elevated, kidney function very good

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Acute exacerbation of arthritis (knee pain): Prescribed Ultram 50 mg every 6 hours as needed. Ordered autoimmune panel. Advised patient to rest. If symptoms persist, will consider further imaging and physical therapy referral.
2. Hypothyroidism: Continue Synthroid. Ordered thyroid panel.
3. Chronic arthritis: Acknowledged limitations due to kidney transplant preventing use of certain anti-inflammatory medications. Will reassess in two weeks and refer to physical therapy if needed.
